title: Rama, Sita and the strong monkey Hanuman.
lines: Long, long ago, in a beautiful kingdom in India called Ayodhya, lived a kind prince.
His name was Rama.
Rama was friendly, brave and honest, and he was very good with his bow and arrow.
Rama was married to Sita.
Sita was beautiful and clever and she loved all the animals and flowers.
And Rama had a brother who was always with him.
His name was Lakshmana.
One day Rama, Sita and Lakshmana had to leave the palace.
They went to live in the big forest, in a little hut made of branches and leaves.
It was quiet and beautiful there.
There were birds and butterflies and flowers.
One day Sita saw something wonderful among the trees.
A deer!
A golden deer, with silver spots, that sparkled in the sun.
Oh, what a beautiful deer, said Sita.
Rama, will you go and find it for me?
Rama went after the deer, and a little later Lakshmana went to look too.
Sita was alone for a moment.
But that golden deer was a trick!
It was a trick by the wicked king Ravana.
Ravana was a giant with ten heads and twenty arms.
He lived on an island far away in the sea, the island of Lanka.
Ravana came flying in a flying chariot, and he took Sita far away to his island.
When Rama and Lakshmana came back, Sita was gone.
Rama was so sad.
Sita!
he called.
Where are you?
Rama and Lakshmana went looking.
They searched and searched, through forests and over mountains.
And one day they came to a land full of monkeys.
There they met a very special monkey.
His name was Hanuman.
Hanuman was the strongest monkey in the whole world.
He had a long tail and he could jump very high.
Hanuman said: Rama, I will help you.
I will find Sita!
Hanuman stood at the edge of the sea.
He made himself big, bigger and bigger, as big as a mountain.
And then he jumped!
He jumped over the whole sea, all the way to the island of Lanka.
There he searched everywhere.
And in a beautiful garden, under a tree, he found Sita.
She was alone and sad.
Hanuman gave her Rama's ring.
Sita, Rama is coming to get you, he whispered.
Don't be afraid.
Sita smiled for the first time in a long time.
Hanuman jumped back over the sea and told Rama everything.
But how could Rama get to the island?
The sea was so big.
The monkeys had an idea.
Let's build a bridge!
Thousands of monkeys carried stones to the sea.
They wrote Rama's name on every stone, and look: the stones floated!
Stone after stone, day after day, the monkeys built a long bridge across the sea.
Rama, Lakshmana, Hanuman and all the monkeys walked across the bridge to the island.
Rama fought bravely against the wicked king Ravana, with his bow and arrow.
And good won over bad.
Rama and Sita saw each other again, and they gave each other a big hug.
Then they went back home, to Ayodhya.
It was a dark night, with no moon.
But the people of Ayodhya wanted Rama and Sita to find their way home.
So they put lights everywhere.
Little oil lamps, in front of every house, on every roof, along every road.
Thousands of lights!
The whole land was shining.
Everyone was happy and danced and sang.
And do you know what?
Every year people still light little lamps, to celebrate that Rama and Sita came home, and that light wins over darkness.
That festival is called Diwali.
